criteria.text: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient is an adult (at least 18 years old).
Patient has tried metformin ER (generic Glucophage XR).
Documented allergy to an inert ingredient in generic Glucophage XR that is not present in the requested Fortamet or Glumetza (or respective generic).
An FDA MedWatch report has been completed and submitted for the adverse event with generic Glucophage XR.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Metformin ER: PA scope is generics for Fortamet and Glumetza. Generic Glucophage XR is the preferred step. Extended-release tablet strengths: Fortamet 500 mg/1000 mg; Glucophage XR 500 mg/750 mg; Glumetza 500 mg/1000 mg.
Grandfathering for current users of brand or generic Fortamet or Glumetza is not permitted. All initial criteria apply. Denial criteria are the inverse of the three required approval conditions.

Reauthorization (notes only): must meet all initial criteria, have documented positive clinical response, and documented better tolerance of the requested generic Fortamet or Glumetza than generic Glucophage XR. Documentation requires manual review.
Authorization (notes only): initial up to 6 months; reauthorization up to 1 year.
Quantity limits (notes only): Fortamet 2 tablets/day; Glumetza 2 tablets/day.

Pharmacokinetics (notes only): source describes product-specific peak concentrations, exposure, food effects and dose proportionality. Mechanism (notes only): metformin reduces hepatic glucose production and intestinal glucose absorption and improves peripheral insulin sensitivity. Pharmacokinetics, mechanism and package-insert references remain in the full archived source text; they are not approval predicates.
Source: Version 1; Last updated 4/7/2016; Approved 4/29/2016; Effective for Dates of Service 10/3/2016 and thereafter. Rules engine is the sole eligibility evaluator.
